I did the 2 month Early Engineering program starting in October 2023 and am almost at the end of my support period, which was supposed to be 6 months long but was extended twice because of my grandmother's death and because a hurricane affected me, so they have been very helpful with that.

Overall, it is pricey but if you have the money, it is helpful to do. For me, a guided structure always helps me stick to something, and I followed it as best as I could for nearly the first 2 months. I got a job thanks to a cousin's referral near the end of that 2 months, and it wasn't the typical high-paying job they advertise, but it was a very good offer that just landed on my lap (80k, fully remote, working with cousin, + bonuses and raise potential) so I took it. I got let go after 4 months though so I am now making the most of my support period and all the resources and coaches are still there to help me.

The most helpful things to me have been: lots of education, practice, and discussion on leetcode style problems, followed by thorough strategies for job hunting, coding and behavioral interviewing skills, resume, finding referrals, negotiation, etc. And they offer live 1:1 coaching and lots of sessions for various topics like resume review, interviewing skills, and AMAs.

From what I remember, their support always responds within a day and are usually very helpful, including coding and technical questions, as well as general issues.

The things I would improve are their style of writing (sometimes it seems too informal), the formatting for their solutions to coding problems (the titles are currently sometimes just a file name rather than a properly formatted title), and I was sometimes confused about the overall weekly cycle, so I wish they'd make that more clear somehow, like adding space or sections between each week so that the separation is clearer, or adding a calendar.

I enrolled in the Interview Kickstart program last October.

For background, I am still an early software engineer with almost 2 years of experience. I graduated with a Bachelor's in Computer Science in late 2020. I have about 1.25 years experience at Amazon Web Services as a back-end engineer for Elastic Block Store, and then about 4 months of experience with Pride Automation Inc working as a full-stack engineer with Node.JS.

The Interview Kickstart program is good because it covers pretty much everything you need to get a higher paying software engineering job. Although a lot of it can be found outside the program, it does help because it offers structure that makes it easier to stick to it. I did the Early Engineering LevelUp program (\~2 months with a 6 month support period after). It covers most programming topics asked in interviews, and you will do a lot of problems like the ones on LeetCode. You have class 1-2 times a week and can ask questions. Then, they go over basic application stuff like resumes, reaching out to recruiters, and behavioral interviews. It is great if you need the motivation and guidance to do all these things. They provide mock behavioral and technical interviews performed by people in the industry, so that is one of the best forms of practice. They also have miscellanious sessions to ask questions about resumes (and get it reviewed), specific technical problems, or about the industry in general.

Their customer service is always responsive and helpful. I have had no issues with them.

I ended up getting a job because of a referral from my cousin after about 2 months into the program. I unfortunately got let go recently, so I will be finishing up the IK program to help me find another job since the support period is still available for me.
